subject: ValenBank VM packet and pen-test summary / follow-up
body:
From: Jamie Lin <jamie.lin@valenbank.com>

Cc: RiskOps Purchasing <procurement@valenbank.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ValenBank VM questionnaire — SBOM, pen-test, patch SLAs

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the initial RFP packet. Procurement and our security team had a couple of follow-ups specifically around vulnerability management:

- SAST / DAST coverage: which tools and cadence do you use, and do you provide raw scan outputs or triage summaries?
- Patch SLAs: for critical CVEs affecting your hosted runtime, what are your target remediation windows and how do you communicate mitigations?
- Pen test summary: can you provide the latest summary and confirmation of whether any critical or high findings are outstanding?
- SBOM: we need a machine-readable SBOM slice for the runtime components used in hosted Redwood. CSV or SPDX is fine.

If you can send a consolidated evidence packet for procurement review (we're trying to close the security checklist this week), that would be great.

Best,
Jamie Lin
Senior Procurement Manager — ValenBank

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lin <jamie.lin@valenbank.com>
Cc: RiskOps Purchasing <procurement@valenbank.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 11:37:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: ValenBank VM questionnaire — SBOM, pen-test, patch SLAs

Hi Jamie — thanks and appreciate the clear list. Attached is a compact evidence packet to cover the items you listed and to speed procurement review. High level answers below; see attachments for full artefacts.

Attachments in this email:
- redwood-vm-evidence-summary.pdf (high-level answers + timeline table)
- redwood-sbom-inventory-20261011.csv (runtime SBOM slice, columns: component, version, license, origin)
- redwood-patch-sla-table.xlsx (SLA by severity and deployment mode)
- redwood-pentest-summary-2026-09.pdf (summary of most recent engagement)

Quick answers:
- SAST/DAST: We run per-PR SAST (Semgrep + vendor-supplied rules) across all service repos; weekly DAST for hosted runtime (OWASP ZAP + authenticated scans for service endpoints) with triage summaries generated after each scheduled run. Raw scan outputs are available under NDA; triage summaries (false-positive filtered, risk-ranked) are in the attached evidence summary.
- Patch SLAs (hosted): For Redwood-hosted instances we target the following: Critical (CVSS 9.0–10.0) — mitigation work or compensating controls within 72 hours; Critical with active exploit — emergency hotfix within 48 hours. High — 7 calendar days; Medium — 30 calendar days. Dedicated and Private deployments have configurable timelines in the contract; we provide guidance, backport support, and optional managed remediation services. Full SLA table in redwood-patch-sla-table.xlsx.
- Pen test: The September 2026 pen test produced no outstanding critical findings; three high findings were addressed within the agreed 21-day remediation window (see redwood-pentest-summary-2026-09.pdf).
- SBOM: Attached CSV is an export of the runtime SBOM for the hosted control plane and runtime agent. We can also provide SPDX on request.

If you want a one-page artifact with the specific wording to drop into procurement language, say so and Ben/Neha can draft a short clause.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0176

Subject: Re: ValenBank VM questionnaire — SBOM, pen-test, patch SLAs

Jamie / team — adding a bit more technical context on the SAST/DAST and our defect lifecycle so the risk team has specifics to validate:

SAST/Tooling and cadence:
- Primary SAST: Semgrep (rule set: open-source + internal patterns). All PRs and nightly builds run full SAST.
- Secondary: periodic commercial scans for language-specific binaries where relevant (we maintain vendor licenses and results).
- Triage: findings are triaged into our issue tracker (Jira) with automated dedup and severity mapping. Developers have 5 business days to acknowledge P1/P2 security defects; remediation timelines follow the SLA table.

DAST / runtime scanning:
- Weekly authenticated DAST for hosted runtime endpoints (OWASP ZAP with scripted auth flows). Monthly deeper scans run against staging mirrors prior to major releases.
- For findings in DAST we generate reproducible test cases and attach recorded requests/responses to JIRA security tickets.

Evidence retention and exports:
- Triage summaries (CSV + markdown notes) are retained for 12 months; raw scan artifacts retained 90 days unless escalated.
- We can export triage summaries and JIRA references for ValenBank under an attestations NDA.

Patch handling and emergency response:
- If a CVE is patched in a third-party dependency and affects hosted runtime we follow: assess (T0–T4 hrs), mitigation plan (within 24–48 hrs for Critical), deploy fix / workaround (target 72 hrs), and communicate status via status.redwood.ai and to security contacts.
- For Dedicated/Private we provide a remediation runbook and offer managed patching as a billable add-on.

Let me know if you need the exact Semgrep rule-set names or sample triage CSV.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Security Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Hi Jamie — adding the pen-test closure and SBOM delivery notes:

Pen-test summary (high level):
- Engagement: Q3 2026, third-party (BlueWing Security).
- Findings: 0 critical, 3 high (authentication logic, rate-limit bypass scenarios, a deprecated crypto usage flagged in a non-customer-facing admin endpoint). All three have remediation PRs merged as of 2026-09-28; verifications completed and evidence attached in the pen-test PDF.
- Remediation evidence: PR links and verification logs are included in the PDF appendix. We can provide the JIRA ticket numbers and final verification timestamps under NDA.

SBOM and SBOM cadence:
- We generate SBOM exports per release and for each runtime agent build. The attached CSV is a slice of the runtime components relevant to your review.
- We offer an automated SBOM push to customer S3 (or secure share) as part of Dedicated/Private onboarding.

Operational attestations we can provide for procurement:
- Weekly DAST schedules and last three triage summaries (CSV)
- Latest pen-test summary and closure evidence
- Patch SLA table + escalation contacts

If you need a short, procurement-ready paragraph (single bullet) that encapsulates our SLAs and evidence availability, I can draft now and send back.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of AppSec, Redwood Inference
